## Why build it this way

The aim is a site where each claim of a skill comes with evidence that can be checked, a date that can be verified, and an honest account of what generative artificial intelligence (AI) did.

Four decisions follow from that:

1. **Plain text in git.** Every entry is a text file in a public repository, so its full revision history is open. A commit message starting with `publish:` marks a meaningful revision; other commits (typo fixes) are not highlighted.
2. **Checks before publishing.** A script scans every change for NHS numbers and similar identifiers, and blocks data files, before anything is committed.
3. **A required statement of AI use.** Every evidence entry has to say what generative AI did and what was done and checked by hand. The build fails if it is missing.
4. **Nothing is published without review.** Every change is checked and built automatically, but the site only goes live when publishing is started by hand.

## What was built

- A [Quarto](https://quarto.org) website with separate Evidence and Essays listings.
- A filter that adds the AI-use box, the evidence links and a revision-history link to each entry.
- Header validation and a patient-data scan, run before each commit and again during the online build.
- An automatic build on every push, with publishing to GitHub Pages started by hand.

## Next

Version-by-version comparisons on each page, and a skills ledger showing when each skill was first and last evidenced.
